item.title: Council of State strongly criticises Heinen’s income tax reform
item.description:
Council of State strongly criticises Heinen’s income tax reform

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Council of State has delivered a withering verdict on finance minister Eelco Heinen’s plans for a capital gains tax system, saying the proposal had been drawn up too hastily and without proper consideration.

The administrative court said the deadline of 2028 for implementing the law was unrealistic because it would not give the tax office, banks and other institutions time to adapt their systems.

The report from the Council of State, which acts as the government’s constitutional advisor, is the latest setback for the cabinet as it tries to steer its budget for next year through parliament.

Heinen had hoped to speed up the reform of the income tax system to prevent the government losing more money from the current Box 3 mechanism, which the Council of State struck out in 2021 when it ruled that it unfairly discriminated against some savers.

Coalition and opposition parties are divided on how to reform Box 3, the section of the tax return form which calculates the tax due on assets savings based on an estimated rate of return.

D66, CDA and the left-wing opposition parties wanted to formalise this by taxing investors on their actual gains, but Heinen’s party, the right-wing liberal VVD, and opposition groups such as JA21 favour a capital gains tax instead.

€10 billion shortfall

The latter option would create an estimated €10 billion shortfall in the immediate term because assets will not be taxed until they are sold.

The existing mechanism is costing the state €3.5 billion a year in lost revenue because savers can reduce their tax bill if they show their actual returns were lower than the estimated figure, but do not have to pay more if it is higher.

The Council of State criticised the minister’s decision to use a “novelle”, a device that allows legislation to be amended after it has been passed by the Lower House but is still wating to be approved by the senate.

Heinen said that would allow capital gains taxes to be levied on real estate and startup business in 2028 as a stepping-stone towards introducing the tax on all assets from 2030.

But the Council of State said the plans were too complicated, would only affect around 10% of all asset wealth and would have to be enacted at “very high speed”. It would be better to change the entire system in one go in 2030, the report said.

item.title: Drought may be cracking Groningen’s medieval churches
item.description:
Drought may be cracking Groningen’s medieval churches

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Medieval churches in Groningen may be cracking because of drought as well as earthquakes, according to a study reported by broadcaster NOS.

Researchers from water and soil research institute Deltares and the Hanze University of Applied Sciences looked at how drought affects the wierden, man-made dwelling mounds, under churches in Oostum and Den Ham, northwest of the city of Groningen.

The study was commissioned by the province and the Old Groningen Churches Foundation (Stichting Oude Groninger Kerken).

The research began after new damage appeared in the church at Oostum in 2018, two years after suspected earthquake damage there had been repaired. There have been no major quakes in the area since, but the damage appears to be getting worse.

The nave of the Oostum church has stood for 800 years. “It’s not a given that this church will still be here in another 800 years,” researcher Floris Boogaard told NOS, “because it is ageing very fast now.”

Boogaard said lab tests showed the church stands on clay that swells when wet and shrinks during drought, while peat in the ground oxidises and compacts as groundwater levels fall.

He said increased traffic, changes to the surroundings and earthquakes all contribute to cracking, but that drought is the only one of those factors to have changed significantly in recent years, while the cracks have become much worse.

“The climate is changing,” he said. “Dry periods are significantly longer: in 2018 it was dry for two months, and that really does have an effect.” This year also had exceptionally long dry spells and droughts.

The two-year study is still underway, and the researchers say longer-term research is needed before firm conclusions can be drawn. They warn that other historic buildings face the same problem.

Possible solutions are still being examined, but the researchers say the churches need stable water levels around them. At Oostum, pits could be dug around the church to collect rainwater, which would then slowly seep into the ground.

item.title: Banning the infinite scroll: Pro MP files bill on addictive apps
item.description:
Banning the infinite scroll: Pro MP files bill on addictive apps

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Social media platforms, games and dating apps should be banned from using designs like the infinite scroll that keep users online and push them into spending money, according to a bill being submitted to parliament on Monday by Pro MP Barbara Kathmann.

Kathmann told broadcaster NOS her bill would class manipulative features in the design of online platforms as “unfair commercial practices”, which are already illegal under Dutch consumer law. She says the current rules are geared to physical products, but online platforms have become “the new high street or marketplace”.

“If a doll is unsafe, we take it off the market,” she said. “If social media platforms are unsafe, they have to go back to the drawing board and be adapted.”

The proposal also covers chatbots. Kathmann said these products contain tricks “that make us addicted and tempt us into spending money, so that a handful of tech billionaires earn a fortune”.

She would prefer the issue to be tackled at EU level, but that would take too long, and hopes a Dutch law will prompt Brussels to act. She is working with MPs in Germany, France, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Italy and Portugal who want similar legislation.

Last year, a Dutch court ordered Meta to let Instagram and Facebook users in the Netherlands set a chronological, non-algorithmic feed as their default, in a case brought by digital rights group Bits of Freedom. The appeals court upheld the order in March.

item.title: Two men arrested after dinghy with 36 people rescued in Zeeland
item.description:
Two men arrested after dinghy with 36 people rescued in Zeeland

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Border police have arrested two Sudanese men on suspicion of human trafficking after a rubber dinghy containing 38 people was brought ashore on the Dutch coast.

Rescue services were called out to a “suspicious situation” off Zeeuws-Vlaanderen, which borders Belgium, on Saturday morning. They found the boat adrift without a motor near the harbour of Cadzand.

Police said they found jerrycans full of fuel on board, suggesting the motor may have been lost at sea. A spokesman said the rescue operation was carried out to “save people from a distressing situation”.

Media reports said the boat contained 36 migrants, but the Marechaussee, the Dutch border police force, said their identities were under investigation.

One person on board claimed asylum and six were minors. All those on board were taken to the asylum reception centre in Ter Apel, Groningen, later in the day after being checked over by ambulance staff and questioned as witnesses.

Refugee charities said the episode underlined the need to create safe migration routes in Europe. Small boat crossings from the Netherlands are rare, but thousands of people try to reach the UK by sea from France and Belgium every year.

Sofie Croonenberg, an adviser on forced migration at Stichting Vluchteling, told AD.nl: “Human traffickers play a role in this, but the solution lies in expanding safe ways to request asylum in Europe.”

item.title: Prosecutors raise reward for arrest of “Bolle Jos” to €2m
item.description:
Prosecutors raise reward for arrest of “Bolle Jos” to €2m

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch prosecutors have raised the reward for the capture of the convicted drugs baron Jos Leijdekkers, nicknamed “Bolle Jos” or “Chubby Jos”, to €2 million.

The tenfold increase is an attempt to raise the pressure on the 35-year-old, who is believed to be hiding out in Sierra Leone, where Dutch authorities say he is in a relationship with the daughter of president Julius Maada Bio.

Leijdekkers is the most wanted fugitive on Europol’s list of top criminals after Dutch and Belgian courts sentenced him to a total of 103 years in prison in absentia. The reward is the largest of its kind ever offered by the Netherlands.

Two years ago was found guilty in Rotterdam of transporting nearly seven tonnes of cocaine in six shipments, an armed robbery in Finland and ordering an assassination. He has denied all involvement in drug trafficking through his lawyers.

The prosecution service said information leading to his arrest would be handled in strict confidence and not shared with other police forces or the authorities in the west African country.

Dutch justice minister David van Weel said last month that the European Union had withheld €18 million in budget aid to Sierra Leone because of its continued refusal to hand over Leijdekkers.

But the country’s leaders said the payments had been delayed because of “procedural issues” and had nothing to do with the row over Leijdekkers’ extradition.

Earlier Sierra Leone said the Dutch pressure in the case was “scandalous” and accused Van Weel of engaging in “neo-colonialism”.

Chief minister David Moinina Sengeh said: “Hand on heart, our security intelligence does not know where Leijdekkers is. If they know, show the pictures.”

item.title: No sign of deal on budget ahead of crucial week in parliament
item.description:
No sign of deal on budget ahead of crucial week in parliament

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Budget talks between the coalition and opposition parties at the weekend have failed to produce an agreement, meaning the plans will go before parliament this week without majority support.

The coalition parties D66, CDA and VVD had hoped to strike a deal with the opposition before the plans are debated this week, but were unable to find a breakthrough despite speaking to three different combinations.

Prime minister Rob Jetten said at his weekly press conference last Friday that he still wanted to come up with an agreement that balanced the demands of left- and right-wing parties, while the opposition groups have repeatedly urged him to pick a side.

Jetten appeared to be close to securing the support of the left-wing parties Pro and Volt in September after agreeing to abandon €6 billion of welfare spending cuts. But the cabinet is unprepared to meet the two parties’ other demands to raise wealth taxes to make up the shortfall.

Pro leader Jesse Klaver said after meeting Jetten and other coalition leaders in the Catshuis, the prime minister’s official residence, that “there is no political will to work with us”.

“That’s because the cabinet has chosen to give more money to those with the largest fortunes,” Klaver added.

Abortion and surrogacy

Pro and Volt are the only combination that can offer the three coalition parties the votes they need for a majority in both houses of parliament. Jetten also held a video conference with the leaders of three right-wing parties – the farmers’ party BBB, JA21 and the orthodox Protestant SGP.

The parties have drawn up a laundry list of issues where they want the cabinet to make concessions or block legislation, including reforms to facilitate late-term abortions and surrogacy, which the Bible-belt SGP opposes.

The farmers want agriculture minister Jaimi van Essen to scrap his plans to reduce nitrogen pollution by putting up low-emission zones around protected nature areas and offering buyouts to livestock farmers, but none of the coalition parties are prepared to go back to the drawing board.

The three parties said in a statement that they saw “opportunities to talk further”, but there were no signs of a significant shift in their direction. Jetten said on Friday that it was “not sensible” to make the budget vote dependent on non-financial issues.

A third potential route to a majority in the lower house, via the minor parties ChristenUnie and 50Plus, along with the far-right splinter group of former PVV MPs led by Gidi Markuszower, also seemed doomed after ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker came away from talks saying the process was “not going well”.

“We’re doing things we should have sorted out in August,” Bikker said. “And that’s frustrating”.

Jetten warned at his press conference that opposition parties were jeopardising vital measures to ease the cost of living, such as an extension to the discount on fuel duty, if they voted down next year’s budget.

MPs are due to debate the budget measures on Wednesday, with the votes due to take place on November 12.

item.title: Hackers tamper with fridges at 17 Dutch firms as attacks spread
item.description:
Hackers tamper with fridges at 17 Dutch firms as attacks spread

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Hackers tampered with fridges at at least 17 businesses in the Netherlands overnight, Danish manufacturer Danfoss has told broadcaster NOS, as similar attacks hit supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden, including dozens of branches of Albert Heijn’s sister chain Delhaize.

A Danfoss spokesperson told NOS that the Dutch systems targeted were used by businesses including butchers and small neighbourhood shops, but would not name them. None of the Dutch victims is a large supermarket, he said. Albert Heijn also told NOS none of its branches was affected.

One of the businesses impacted was a frozen food storage site. “The systems there are normally set to -20°, but last night we found they were at -10°,” the spokesperson said. “We were able to step in quickly.”

Danfoss advised Dutch customers on October 13 to disconnect the systems from the internet. Those hit overnight were not on a secure network and still used a default password, the spokesperson said.

A Delhaize spokesperson confirmed the hack on Monday morning, newspaper HLN reported, and said shops in both Flanders and Wallonia had been hit. Delhaize, which is calling it an “IT incident”, told NOS that some branches in Luxembourg had also been affected and that it had immediately disconnected its refrigeration systems from the internet.

Carrefour told Flemish broadcaster VRT that 15 of its 700 Belgian stores had been hit. Colruyt said five independently run Spar stores had similar problems, and butcher chain De Laet & Van Haver also reported a sudden rise in temperatures.

RTL Info reported temperatures rising to around 15°, mainly in freezers. Store managers got a text message from Delhaize at around 4am warning them of the problem, and some stores brought in refrigerated lorries to save their stock.

In Belgium, equipment from another manufacturer, Copeland, was also attacked, NOS reported.

In Sweden, supermarket group Ica said a “limited number” of its stores had been affected overnight, and Coop told news agency TT that six of its stores in central Sweden had problems with their refrigeration. One Ica store in southern Sweden said on social media that its fridges and freezers had been set to 50°.

French attack
Last month, on the night of October 11, hackers raised the temperature of refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets, including Intermarché, E.Leclerc and Coopérative U stores, to 50°, destroying fresh and frozen food.

The stores used equipment from Danfoss, which told news agency AFP that most of the affected systems were outdated and no longer received security updates.

Delhaize and Albert Heijn are both owned by Zaandam-based Ahold Delhaize, which reported a cyberattack to Dutch police in October after shutting down several IT systems. Delhaize told NOS it was investigating whether that attack was linked to Monday’s hack.

item.title: Stroopwafel wars: supermarkets slash prices to 34 cents a pack
item.description:
Stroopwafel wars: supermarkets slash prices to 34 cents a pack

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch supermarkets are locked in a price war over stroopwafels, with discount chain Dirk now selling a pack of 12 for 34 cents, Het Parool reports.

That works out at just over 2.8 cents a biscuit, which makes it one of the few food items actually getting cheaper.

Meanwhile, tourists are paying around €13 for a single stroopwafel in central Amsterdam.

In mid-October a pack of Bakker Joop stroopwafels cost 42 cents at Jumbo and 38 cents at Dirk. Albert Heijn was charging 42 cents for a pack of its own brand.

All three have since cut further. Jumbo and Albert Heijn are now at 36 cents, although Albert Heijn’s packs hold only 10 biscuits. That leaves its customers paying the most per waffle, at 3.6 cents each.

Retail expert Paul Moers told the paper that the supermarkets make nothing on the deals, they are so-called “lost leaders” that bring people into the shops, who then inevitably buy other things.

The holdout
Not every chain has joined in. Frisian supermarket Poiesz still charges €1.15 for the same Bakker Joop pack, which earned Moers’ “respect”.

He expects the prices could drop by a few more cents, since the chains are already making heavy losses. Eventually, he said, “the joke will wear off” and the supermarkets will move on to another product.

In Gouda, the stroopwafel’s home town, bakers are unbothered. “It’s comparing apples and oranges,” said Mike van den Berg of Berg’s Bakery and Van Vliet Siroopwafels. “As a baker you have to believe in your product.”

Moers had a final word on the bargain biscuits. They contain no butter, he said, which “says something about how blandening of Dutch taste”.

item.title: Dutch campaigners accuse Philip Morris of heated tobacco fraud
item.description:
Dutch campaigners accuse Philip Morris of heated tobacco fraud

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A criminal complaint is being filed against Phillip Morris for fraud and forgery. A Dutch anti-smoking foundation says it has falsely presented heated tobacco as less harmful than smoking, and broken the ban on advertising tobacco in the Netherlands.

Stichting Rookpreventie Jeugd, a foundation that campaigns against youth smoking, said on Monday it would hand the complaint to the public prosecution service (OM) in mid-November.

The foundation, chaired by former lung specialist Wanda de Kanter, says Philip Morris backs its claims mainly with its own studies and leaves out worrying findings from independent research. It also accuses the company of illegally promoting heated tobacco through specialist shops.

Cancer charity KWF, the lung and heart foundations, the Antoni van Leeuwenhoek cancer institute and the lung doctors’ association NVALT have pledged to back the complaint.

“Since fines from regulators and settlements with bereaved relatives have not stopped Philip Morris from committing new violations, it is now up to criminal law,” lawyer Sjoerd Lopik said in a statement.

In June, doctors and health groups complained to the advertising watchdog about a Philip Morris campaign that used an AI tool to help people object to tougher EU tobacco rules. The Reclame Code Commissie later ruled that the campaign breached the advertising ban.

The foundation’s previous criminal complaint against tobacco makers, filed in 2016, did not lead to a prosecution. A court ruled that regulating the industry was a matter for the government. The foundation says the new complaint is based on breaches of existing law.

item.title: Big wins for PSV and Twente close gap on leaders Feyenoord
item.description:
Big wins for PSV and Twente close gap on leaders Feyenoord

November 2, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Weghorst bags four

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.
